items.question: What was the official cause of death for the chief engineer and third engineer who died in the Stride engine room fire at Barbours Cut, according to the medical examiner?
items.expected_answer: The report does not state a medical cause of death; it says only that local paramedics pronounced the chief engineer and third engineer dead on scene.
items.notes: Tests refusal on an absent detail; the report mentions smoke in the engine control room but gives no autopsy or cause-of-death finding.

items.question: During bunkering of the cargo vessel Stride, what discharge pressure did the tankerman notice on the fuel barge pump after increasing the engine speed to 1,400 rpm?
items.expected_answer: The pump discharge pressure was 90 psi (the barge's maximum allowable pipeline pressure was 100 psi).

evidence.quote: The tankerman slowly increased the engine speed to 1,400 rpm and noticed the discharge pressure of the pump was 90 pounds per square inch ( psi) ( the maximum allowable pipeline pressure on the fuel barge was 100 psi).

items.notes: Tests retrieval of a specific numeric value from the bunkering event sequence.
